description: Hankinnan kohteena oli: Seinäjoen markkinointiviestinnän ytimessä on avaruuden pääkaupunki. Koska Seinäjoki on avaran alueen merkittävin kaupunki, se on avaruuden pääkaupunki. Maantieteellisen avaruuden lisäksi Seinäjoella on tilaa sanan kaikissa merkityksissä: tilaa on kaikelle hyvälle. Avaruuden pääkaupunki kertoo myös asenteestamme. Seinäjoella ollaan rohkeita ja itsevarmoja sekä ylpeitä omasta osaamisesta ja ainutlaatuisuudesta. Me asetamme tavoitteemme korkealle, ja ihailemme myös muita, jotka tekevät niin. Kilpailutuksen tavoitteena on löytää kumppani strategiseen ja kokonaisvaltaiseen markkinoinnin ja viestinnän suunnitteluun sekä avaruuden pääkaupunki -konseptin nostamiseen seuraavalle tasolle. Kumppanin tehtävä on suunnitella yhdessä tilaajan kanssa markkinoinnin isot suuntaviivat tuleville vuosille niin, että tilaajan strategiset tavoitteet saavutettaisiin. Kumppanilta odotetaan kokonaisnäkemystä ja laajaa mahdollisuuksien tunnistamista markkinoinnin ja viestinnän käytettävissä olevista keinoista sekä ymmärrystä siitä, kuinka kokonaisbudjetti käytetään parhaalla hinta-laatusuhteella. Kumppanin odotetaan tarjoavan myös näkemystä viestintäkärkien määrittämiseen markkinoinnin systemaattisuuden varmistamiseksi. Haemme kumppania kampanjoiden suunnitteluun ja toteutukseen, mainoskampanjoiden hallintaan markkinointikanavissa sekä kampanjoiden tulosten raportointiin ja analysointiin. Toteutukset sisältävät digitaalisia ja painettuja toteutuksia sekä graafista suunnittelua. Haemme kumppania myös Seinäjoen kaupungin ja avaruuden pääkaupungin visuaalisen ilmeen uudistamiseen. title: Germany – Foreign economic-aid-related services – 10040386-Mejorar mecanismos políticos, técnicos y financieros para escalar la gestión sostenible de suelos en Bolivia
description: In the Bolivian High Plateau ("Altiplano") rural families rely on agriculture, livestock farming, and other economic activities -such as tourism and trade- to sustain their livelihoods. However, an acute soil degradation, frosts, droughts, hailstorms, and strong winds reduce productivity and increase the vulnerability of rural communities. Compounding this issue is migration to urban centres and other regions from youth and women. According to the National Institute of Statistics (INE, 2025), more than 50% of rural families in the Altiplano live under poverty line, with limited access to technical, financial, and innovation services. All these factors result in greater vulnerability to climate change and a reduced adaptive capacity. In response Bolivia committed to achieve Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) by 2030 through soil restoration, climate resilience, and biodiversity conservation; under the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD). Sustainable soil management is a fundamental pillar for restoring soil health and strengthening agrifood systems and ecosystems resilience. Hence, the German Cooperation together with national subnational stakeholders, producers and civil society organizations will implement the Sustainable Soil Management for agrifood system adaptation and resilience Project (SUAGRI) to foster soil management through a comprehensive approach. This approach includes strengthening the political, regulatory, and institutional framework; developing a soil information and monitoring system; fostering soil technological innovation; managing bioinputs; and ensuring access to public and private financing mechanisms to farmers. SUAGRI aims to improve and consolidate the political, regulatory, technical, and financial enable conditions to scale up sustainable soil management and biodiversity restoration in the Bolivian Altiplano. Thus, it contributes to increase agrifood systems and ecosystems resilience improving the livelihoods of households. SUAGRI proposes four components, described below: 1. Political and Regulatory Instruments: Improve norms and policy instruments to strengthen the regulatory framework, guiding territorial planning and public investments toward sustainable agricultural production. Through a participatory and multisectoral approach that brings together public, private, and local actors, it promotes policy coherence, inter-institutional coordination, and the integration of environmental, social, and economic criteria. 2. Soil Geoinformation: Generate and facilitate soil-related information to strengthen the availability, quality, and access to technical and scientific information for sustainable soil management. This enables better territorial and natural resource management. It also promotes the integration of traditional knowledge, with an emphasis on the participation of women and youth. 3. Financial mechanisms: Facilitate access to public and private financial mechanisms to scale up soil restoration and resilient agricultural production. This component is aimed at producers: micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), the private sector, and civil society organizations. . 4. Integrated Bioinputs Management: To increase the supply and demand for bio-inputs (such as compost, humus, among others), under sustainability criteria that contribute to soil recovery and health; biodiversity; and resilient agricultural production. This will be done with the participation of producer organizations and MSMEs, led primarily by women and rural youth.

title: MINIATURISED L-BAND FILTER - EXPRO+
description: The European Space Agency's (ESA) Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity (SMOS) mission, launched in November 2009 under the Earth Explorers program, continues to deliver high-quality global maps of soil moisture and ocean surface salinity. Its payload, the Microwave Imaging Radiometer with Aperture Synthesis (MIRAS), is an L-band interferometric radiometer that achieves unprecedented resolution [RD 1 - RD 5]. However, the image reconstruction process still exhibits spatial ripple errors caused by antenna pattern variations between receivers, independent of radiometric noise or modelling inaccuracies. These variations significantly impact reconstruction accuracy, especially when the inter-element spacing exceeds the Nyquist alias-free limit, as seen in SMOS. To address these limitations, extensive research has explored alternative antenna configurations designed to enhance image quality through alias-free array designs while improving spatial resolution [RD 6-RD 9]. Proposed antenna arrays feature a large number of closely spaced, dual-polarizedradiating elements. Each polarization has dedicated receive chains that amplify and filter signals, down-convert them to IF frequencies, and digitize them as complex samples. The combination of dense element spacing and numerous receiver components necessitates miniaturization. A critical component of the receiver is the high-performance RF filter, which must provide effective out-of-band interference suppression while maintaining a uniform and reproducible transfer function across all units. Currently, coaxial resonator filters fulfil this role; however, their bulkiness conflicts with the receiver's miniaturization requirements.Several alternative technologies, including SAW, BAW, SIW, and dielectric filters, offer significant potential for size reduction while maintaining performance. Since the RF filter is positioned after the low-noise amplifier, insertion loss is not a primary design constraint. This flexibility allows for innovative design approaches, such as pre-distortion techniques and lossy filter theory, to further enhance efficiency and integration.The objective of this activity is to design and experimentally validate miniaturized filters for L-band radiometers operating within the 1400-1427 MHz frequency band, satisfying SMOS or equivalent specifications. Two breadboard prototypes,implementing alternative technological approaches, will be designed. A manufacturing run of at least six units per design, yieldinga minimum of twelve units, will be followed by rigorous performance validation testing.The activity aims to reach TRL 4.
